AREG800A automotive radar echo generation supports instantaneous IF bandwidths of 1 GHz, 2 GHz, or 5 GHz, with IF frequency ranges up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on option configuration [40].
Its RF radar-related bands include 24 GHz to 24.25 GHz, 24 GHz to 44 GHz, and 76 GHz to 81 GHz [40].
QAT100 with AREG800A covers 76 GHz to 77 GHz and 77 GHz to 81 GHz, with 4 GHz RF instantaneous bandwidth [37].
AREG800A ghost-object suppression is measured using a vector network analyzer in time domain, with 125 kHz frequency step size, 100 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power, and spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on bandwidth [2].
AREG800A IF transfer measurements specify VNA conditions of 2.5 MHz frequency step size, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power, and spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on bandwidth [3].
AREG8-81S / AREG8-81D RF transfer characteristics use 2.5 MHz frequency step size, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, Hann normal gate, bandpass filter type, and measurement from RX waveguide input to TX waveguide output connector [36].
ZNB3000 VNAs provide 1 Hz frequency resolution, 1 to 100001 measurement points per trace, and 1 Hz to 1 MHz measurement bandwidth as base units, extendable to 1 Hz to 10 MHz with the ZNB3-K17 option [60].
ZNB3000 frequency ranges extend from 9 kHz to 43.5 GHz as base models and up to 54.0 GHz with frequency upgrade options [20].
ZNA VNAs cover up to 67 GHz across the ZNA26, ZNA43, ZNA50, and ZNA67 models [33].
ZNA67EXT is a 1.0 mm VNA system covering 10 MHz to 110 GHz, with 1 Hz frequency resolution, 1 to 100001 measurement points, and 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz measurement bandwidths [29].
【推論】As automotive radar test spans increase from 1 GHz toward 5 GHz IF bandwidth, the VNA must support the corresponding sweep span, fine frequency stepping such as 125 kHz or 2.5 MHz, and measurement bandwidths such as 100 kHz or 1 kHz used in the AREG800A measurements.[2][3][40]
【推論】Because ghost-object suppression is measured with a VNA in time domain, automotive radar validation can require VNA time-domain analysis rather than only frequency-domain S-parameter measurement.[2]

AREG800A automotive radar echo generation supports instantaneous IF bandwidths of 1 GHz, 2 GHz, or 5 GHz, with IF frequency ranges up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on option configuration [40].
Its RF radar-related bands include 24 GHz to 24.25 GHz, 24 GHz to 44 GHz, and 76 GHz to 81 GHz [40].
QAT100 with AREG800A covers 76 GHz to 77 GHz and 77 GHz to 81 GHz, with 4 GHz RF instantaneous bandwidth [37].
AREG800A ghost-object suppression is measured using a vector network analyzer in time domain, with 125 kHz frequency step size, 100 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power, and spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on bandwidth [2].
AREG800A IF transfer measurements specify VNA conditions of 2.5 MHz frequency step size, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power, and spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on bandwidth [3].
AREG8-81S / AREG8-81D RF transfer characteristics use 2.5 MHz frequency step size, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, Hann normal gate, bandpass filter type, and measurement from RX waveguide input to TX waveguide output connector [36].
ZNB3000 VNAs provide 1 Hz frequency resolution, 1 to 100001 measurement points per trace, and 1 Hz to 1 MHz measurement bandwidth as base units, extendable to 1 Hz to 10 MHz with the ZNB3-K17 option [60].
ZNB3000 frequency ranges extend from 9 kHz to 43.5 GHz as base models and up to 54.0 GHz with frequency upgrade options [20].
ZNA VNAs cover up to 67 GHz across the ZNA26, ZNA43, ZNA50, and ZNA67 models [33].
ZNA67EXT is a 1.0 mm VNA system covering 10 MHz to 110 GHz, with 1 Hz frequency resolution, 1 to 100001 measurement points, and 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz measurement bandwidths [29].
【推論】As automotive radar test spans increase from 1 GHz toward 5 GHz IF bandwidth, the VNA must support the corresponding sweep span, fine frequency stepping such as 125 kHz or 2.5 MHz, and measurement bandwidths such as 100 kHz or 1 kHz used in the AREG800A measurements.[2][3][40]
【推論】Because ghost-object suppression is measured with a VNA in time domain, automotive radar validation can require VNA time-domain analysis rather than only frequency-domain S-parameter measurement.[2]
